title: Mid-sprint Rollout Playback Notes - Console Tooling
content:
Meeting: Mid-sprint rollout playback for console tooling
Date: 2026-05-21
Facilitator: Maya Chen
Attendees: Donovan, Priya, Samir, Lena, QA on-call (Jon), SRE rotation (Avery)
Duration: 45m

Agenda:
- Quick state of the canary (metrics + failures)
- UI behavior observed by field QA and telemetry divergence
- Rollout guardrail checks and thresholds
- Short-term mitigation + decision on rollback vs. pause
- Action items and owner commitments

Notes / Observations:
- Canary (v3.2.1) started at 09:10 PT. Traffic slice: 5%. Initial latency looks fine (p50 ~ 120ms), but after ~18m p95 spikes to ~980ms in east-us region.
- Root suspect: prefix caching regression in the new batching layer. Suspect change in PR #812 that altered cache key normalization when client-supplied metadata is present.
- Field QA found a UI regression: conversation threading occasionally drops prompt context when switching model variants. Repro steps captured in CON-4237. Repro rate low but correlated with the same traffic pattern that produced latency spikes.
- Telemetry: two signals correlate — increased token generation retries and an uptick in 'cache-miss' events for prefill segments. SRE flagged transient pod OOMs in the same time window (node metrics attached to Confluence playback).
- Canary did not fully fail; some users experienced timeouts (~2-3% of canary requests) which triggered automated alerting and reduced the traffic slice from 5% to 2% by the fallback policy.

Decisions made:
- Pause the canary expansion and do not proceed to 20% until a fix for cache key normalization lands. (Decision owner: Maya)
- Create a targeted rollback plan if repro appears at >=3% error rate across two regions. (Decision owner: Donovan)
- Treat UI thread-drop bug as P1 for this week given customer-visible data loss on model context. (Decision owner: Priya)

Action items:
- Samir: create a minimal repro harness for the cache-key change and test locally against v3.2.1 branch. Due: 2026-05-24. Linked PR: github PR #812.
- Priya: triage CON-4237, add clear reproduction steps and attach a short screen capture from field QA. Due: 2026-05-22.
- Donovan: draft the rollback runbook with exact k8s commands and traffic-slice rollback thresholds. Include smoke tests. Due: 2026-05-23.
- Lena: add an observability dashboard tile that surfaces prefix-cache miss rate (per region) and an alert at 0.5% sustained over 5m. Due: 2026-05-22.
- QA (Jon): exercise the canary with session-switch permutations to validate the UI fix after PR patch. Add test scenarios to the nightly e2e matrix. Due: 2026-05-25.
- SRE (Avery): review pod memory requests/limits for canary pool and propose guardrail adjustments if OOMs persist. Due: 2026-05-24.

Open questions / Risks:
- Is the cache key normalization change compatible with the KV cache layout used by older client SDKs? Need to confirm backwards compatibility. (Risk owner: Samir)
- Latency spike pattern appears tied to a specific sequence-length distribution in requests — do we have synthetic load that mirrors the exact token length mix? (Action: Jonathan from perf to provide a trace mix)
- Could the UI thread-drop be a symptom of the same prefix-caching mismatch rather than a separate bug? If so, a single fix may address both.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- If we patch the cache normalization, add a feature flag toggle so we can revert quickly without a full rollback.
- Consider adding a short-lived telemetry tag to canary traffic so we can filter events by rollout id and client SDK version in dashboards.

Appendix (quick metrics snapshot):
- Canary traffic: 5% -> auto-reduced to 2% at 09:34 PT
- Error rate (5xx/timeouts): peaked at 2.9% between 09:28-09:36 PT
- p95 latency: baseline 210ms -> spike 980ms
- Cache miss rate (prefill segment): baseline 6% -> 18% during spike

References:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-console/pull/812
- Jira: CON-4237 (UI thread drop)
- Playbook: Rollout Playbook (Confluence)
- Slack thread: #console-rollouts (linked in linked_artifacts)

Next sync: 2026-05-22 10:00 PT (short check-in to confirm repro status and decide patch vs rollback)

End of notes.
